description: burrow_run_lost on gke-live: first dispatch of warren-42f1 (run_2ty68jhvnvcb) was lost by the runtime ~8 min in; work discarded. Immediate re-dispatch with the identical prompt succeeded. Pattern: treat burrow_run_lost as infra, not agent failure — re-dispatch immediately, do not re-scope the prompt.
resolution: Re-dispatched same prompt (run_070b3421rpmg) -> PR #775 merged. Filed warren-30eb to classify the loss and consider one auto-retry at reap.

name: dogfood-pipeline-sequential-merge-gates
description: Dogfood pipeline round 2 (pl-882c, 14 issues, PRs #773-#786): sequential dispatch with merge gates completes a 14-child dependency plan in one session. Costs: kimi-k3 issue runs $0.26-$3.84 (big refactors 45-51 min), conflict-repair runs $0.10-$0.60. Every PR that outlived another merge went DIRTY on .seeds/issues.jsonl — repair-run-on-branch resolved 6/6 with zero lost seed closes when the prompt names both sides' close states explicitly. GitHub mergeability reads UNKNOWN for ~1 min after a repair push; re-check before diagnosing.

Warren run pods re-baseline bundle budgets ~1.3-1.5KB gzip LOWER than CI for identical source — the agent image toolchain gzips cooler than CI, and 'rm -rf src/ui/node_modules' does NOT fix it (proven by run_hk0cva2nbx09: wrote 195795, CI measured 197140). Every pod-written budget then fails CI, and since lowering always applies, pods actively corrupt correct budgets.
resolution: Never trust a pod-written bundle budget. Re-baseline from a CI-matching machine (laptop clean build == CI byte-for-byte), or for a many-PR UI plan push a documented session headroom bump to main once and have the final sweep ratchet down from a LOCAL clean build. Filed warren-6397.

description: GLM-5.3/openrouter on pi hung mid-turn (no stream data) for 45min; warren watchdog (heartbeatTimeoutMs 45min) eventually killed it at $2.38 with work discarded. A later socket-close during a turn WAS caught instantly as provider_error and auto-retried by the provider-retry consumer — only the silent-hang case burns money.
resolution: Filed warren-1f85 (turn-level inactivity abort + salvage-before-destroy for timed_out). When re-dispatching a big server-side task after a hang, add concrete file-size/scope guidance to the prompt — the re-dispatch of warren-1b40 with the route-table 500-line hint finished in 18min at $0.49.

name: dogfood-max-parallel-pr-shepherding
description: Dogfood pipeline max-parallel PR shepherding (pl-3ce8 13 issues + pl-4ab6 25 issues, 2026-08-27): dispatch every unblocked issue at once, then treat PR merge as a serial drain — after EVERY merge to main, batch-heal all open sibling branches in one worktree loop (git merge origin/main; budgets conflict -> take main's; .seeds merges via driver; verify check:seeds-integrity; push) and re-arm auto-merge. For bundle budgets under many parallel UI PRs, one documented headroom bump pushed straight to main kills the per-PR budget chase; the plan's final sweep ratchets it back down. ~24 heal cycles for 25 PRs; zero lost seed closes.

glm-5.3-flash on pi/openrouter intermittently degenerates: reasoning stream emits endless newline tokens until stopReason=length (reasoning ~4095 of 4096 output tokens), turn after turn, so the agent stages work but never commits — runs die as dropped_commit/noChanges. Hit 5 of 22 runs in the pl-096b session (~$4 wasted). Also produces analysis-paralysis runs (36 read-only tool calls, zero writes).
resolution: Two prompt-level mitigations that worked: (1) commit-discipline addendum — 'commit after EVERY unit of work; commits are the only thing that survives' (fixed e361 attempt 2); (2) hard scaffold for complex issues — 'AT MOST 8 exploration tool calls, then write your first file' plus an explicit file-by-file implementation plan (fixed 0ad3 attempt 3). For dropped_commit, re-dispatch seeded from the salvage rescue ref (see companion pattern record). Filed warren-74a7 for a harness-level abort.

name: rescue-ref-seeded-redispatch
description: Rescue-ref-seeded re-dispatch recovers dropped_commit work cheaply: prompt the retry run to 'git fetch origin warren/rescue/run_<id>; git checkout FETCH_HEAD -- .; commit IMMEDIATELY', then review-fix-complete. Recovered warren-326f for $0.37 and warren-c7f5 for $2.22 on first retry after fresh attempts failed. Check the rescue diff first (git diff origin/main FETCH_HEAD --stat) — only seed from it when additions are substantial; a mostly-deletions diff just means an old base (warren-0ad3's 36-line rescue was not worth it, fresh scaffolded dispatch won instead).

name: parallel-same-extension-dispatch-shepherding
description: Parallel same-extension dispatch (8 runs on campaign-controller, pl-096b) is workable but every PR conflicts on the same seams: .seeds/issues.jsonl (always), store/schema.ts migrations (renumber to follow main's highest), store/events.ts + reconcile/reconciler.ts (union imports/steps). Shepherding cost: ~6 driver-aware heals + 3 repair runs for 14 PRs. Repair runs on the PR branch handled semantic conflicts well (e.g. renumbering migrations, binding new mandatory mutation flags into main-side fixtures after warren-094b). GitHub mergeability (CLEAN/DIRTY) lagged repeatedly in BOTH directions mid-chase — trust git merge-tree + branch tips, and re-check before spending a repair run.

K8s cost-cap cancel destroys committed work (warren-01d5): run_d1y23g1vsdj6 was killed at $5.05/$5 cap ~2 min before clean completion with 3 commits + 37 passing tests in the workspace; the pod reached terminal phase without finalize/salvage, reap logged branch_push_failed, work unrecoverable. Per-run caps must include headroom for final verification, and cost-cap termination needs the graceful-cancel salvage path.
resolution: Filed warren-01d5 (P1); retried via new campaign with flat budget

name: campaign-budget-amendment
description: Campaign per-run budget neutralized by amendment: perRunUsd is schema-required and positive, so 'no per-run cap' = perRun == daily == total (ame-kill-per-run-cap on camp-openclaw-131847-r2, flat $15). Amendments cannot change an in-flight run's cap — warren fixes maxCostUsd at dispatch with no mid-run raise API. Amendment apply via CLI was broken (warren-04a6, fixed f3fd3e9b); the in-pod workaround is calling applyAmendment directly with the raw JSON.

name: campaign-retry-after-infra-loss
description: Campaign retry after infra loss: no re-attempt exists (warren-f411 open) — a failed work item completes the campaign. Recovery pattern proven on openclaw #131847: import a new campaign (camp-<issue>-r2) whose prompt embeds the lost attempt's validated design as PROVEN APPROACH plus BUDGET DISCIPLINE (stop at green tests); retry succeeded at $2.43 vs the lost $5.05 attempt, PR openclaw/openclaw#132081 opened by the controller with the evidence gate green natively via the profile PR-body contract.

Dogfood polling loops: in zsh, 'for r in $RUNS' with RUNS='id1 id2 id3' does NOT word-split — the loop runs once with all ids as one word, curl gets a garbage URL, and the poll prints empty lines that a lenient parser reads as 'not terminal yet', spinning to the iteration cap (observed 3x, 2026-08-28 P1 session). Same silent-spin family as the .run envelope bare-parse trap.
resolution: Write literal run ids into the loop (or a real array); guard every poll line with ${line:-EMPTY-RESPONSE} so a transport failure prints loudly instead of blank. Also stash the API token in a file first — background task shells don't inherit foreground kubectl context reliably.

name: parallel-p1-dispatch-collision-cost
description: 2026-08-28 P1 session: three independent P1s dispatched in PARALLEL (glm-5.3-flash on pi/openrouter, $2.68 total). Collision cost was low: two PRs (#1174, #1175) auto-merged untouched; only the slowest (#1176) went DIRTY on .seeds/issues.jsonl and needed the warren-b34b driver-aware worktree merge (merge origin/main --no-verify in a throwaway worktree, check:seeds-integrity, push — ~3 min). Parallel is fine for small independent batches when you budget one seeds-driver merge for every PR that outlives another's merge. Also observed: a concurrent operator session had locally broadened a dispatched issue's scope via uncommitted sd update while the run closed the original scope — reconcile by filing the broadened scope as a NEW issue (warren-1fa6) and discarding the stale local edit, never by reopening the closed row.
